nodes.summary: Foundry DataModel defining a schema for an array of skill entries (enabled, skill name, proficiency) used to validate the skill picker form.

nodes.name: KingdomSkillPicker
nodes.summary: FormApp subclass rendering an XY grid of kingdom skills with enable/proficiency toggles; calls onSave callback with the selected skill-to-rank mapping on confirmation.

nodes.name: ModifyCampaignClock.kt
nodes.summary: Implements the ModifyCampaignClock FormApp dialog for creating or editing a campaign clock, capturing label, turn counts, expiry consequences, and pause behaviour.

nodes.name: ModifyCampaignClockDataModel
nodes.summary: Foundry DataModel schema for the campaign clock form, validating label, turn counts, description, pause flag, unrest consequence, and expiry message.

nodes.name: ModifyCampaignClock
nodes.summary: FormApp that presents create/edit UI for a CampaignClock, auto-generating a UUID for new clocks and invoking an afterSubmit callback on save.

nodes.name: ModifyCharter.kt
nodes.summary: Implements the ModifyCharter FormApp dialog for creating or editing a kingdom charter, including ability boost/flaw selection and free-boost count.

nodes.name: ModifyCharterDataModel
nodes.summary: Foundry DataModel schema for charter form fields including id, name, description, nullable boost/flaw enums, and free-boost count.

nodes.name: ModifyCharter
nodes.summary: FormApp for creating or editing a RawCharter; slugifies the id on submit and routes the validated charter data back via an afterSubmit callback.

nodes.name: ModifyFeat.kt
nodes.summary: Implements the ModifyFeat FormApp dialog for creating or editing a kingdom feat, covering level, resource dice, magic item level increase, anarchy limit, ruin threshold increases, and roll options.

nodes.name: ModifyFeatDataModel
nodes.summary: Foundry DataModel schema for the feat form, covering id, name, descriptive text, level, numeric bonus fields, and optional roll-option string.

nodes.name: ModifyFeat
nodes.summary: FormApp for creating or editing a RawFeat; assembles the ruin-threshold increase array from two numeric inputs and calls afterSubmit with the resulting data.

nodes.name: ModifyGovernment.kt
nodes.summary: Implements the ModifyGovernment FormApp dialog for creating or editing a kingdom government type, including ability boosts, skill proficiencies, and a required bonus feat selection.

nodes.name: ModifyGovernmentDataModel
nodes.summary: Foundry DataModel schema for government form fields: id, name, description, bonusFeat, freeBoosts, and boolean arrays for skill proficiencies and ability boosts.

nodes.name: ModifyGovernment
nodes.summary: FormApp for creating or editing a RawGovernment; zips boolean arrays with KingdomAbility and KingdomSkill entries to reconstruct the boost and skill-proficiency lists on submit.

nodes.name: ModifyHeartland.kt
nodes.summary: Implements the ModifyHeartland FormApp dialog for creating or editing a kingdom heartland entry, capturing id, name, description, and a single ability boost.

nodes.name: ModifyHeartlandDataModel
nodes.summary: Foundry DataModel schema for heartland form fields: id, name, description, and a KingdomAbility boost enum.

nodes.name: ModifyHeartland
nodes.summary: FormApp for creating or editing a RawHeartland; slugifies the id and calls afterSubmit with the completed heartland data.

nodes.name: ModifyKingdomEvent.kt
nodes.summary: Implements the ModifyKingdomEvent FormApp dialog for authoring kingdom events, covering traits, stage skills, leader assignment, modifier, and all four outcome message fields.

nodes.name: ModifyKingdomEventDataModel
nodes.summary: Foundry DataModel schema for kingdom event form fields including id, name, description, trait booleans, modifier, leader enum, and outcome message strings.

nodes.name: ModifyKingdomEvent
nodes.summary: FormApp for authoring or editing a RawKingdomEvent; the 'edit-skills' action spawns a nested KingdomSkillPicker to assign applicable skills to the first event stage.

nodes.name: ModifyMilestone.kt
nodes.summary: Implements the ModifyMilestone FormApp dialog for creating or editing a kingdom milestone, capturing its id, name, and XP reward.

nodes.name: ModifyMilestoneDataModel
nodes.summary: Foundry DataModel schema for milestone form fields: id, name, and XP integer.

nodes.name: ModifyMilestone
nodes.summary: FormApp for creating or editing a RawMilestone; preserves completed/enabledOnFirstRun/isCultMilestone flags across edits and calls afterSubmit on save.

nodes.name: PickEvent.kt
nodes.summary: Provides the pickEvent suspend function presenting a dropdown of ongoing kingdom events with settlement-context suffixes, returning the selected OngoingEvent or null if none are active.

nodes.name: PickEventSettlement.kt
nodes.summary: Provides the pickEventSettlement suspend function that prompts the user to select a settlement and indicate secret-location status when assigning a kingdom event to a specific scene.

nodes.name: PickLeader.kt
nodes.summary: Provides the pickLeader suspend function that presents an enum-driven dropdown to select one of the eight leader roles.

nodes.name: PopulationDialogs.kt
nodes.summary: Implements PopulationAddDialog and PopulationEditDialog, two SimpleApp dialogs for adding and editing NPC entries in a settlement's population roster.

nodes.name: PopulationAddDialog
nodes.summary: SimpleApp dialog for adding a new NPC to a settlement population roster, reading DOM inputs directly and generating a random id for the new entry.

nodes.name: PopulationEditDialog
nodes.summary: SimpleApp dialog for editing or deleting an existing NPC entry; falls back to the existing values if the user leaves fields blank.

nodes.name: RequestAmount.kt
nodes.summary: Provides the requestAmount suspend function that shows a minimal numeric-input prompt and returns the entered integer, defaulting to 1.

nodes.name: SettlementSizeHelp.kt
nodes.summary: Provides the settlementSizeHelp suspend function that opens a read-only reference table of settlement size tiers with blocks, population, level, consumption, item bonus, and influence data.

nodes.name: StructureXpDialog.kt
nodes.summary: Provides the structureXpDialog suspend function that lets the GM pick a structure from the compendium and computes the XP reward (doubled for edifice-trait structures).

nodes.name: Icons.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the createKingmakerIcon function that registers a Foundry party-actor toolbar icon linking to the kingdom sheet via the action dispatcher.

nodes.name: Kingdom.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the KingdomActor typealias for PF2EParty and provides getKingdom/setKingdom/clearKingdom extension functions for reading and writing KingdomData stored as actor flags.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Kotlin extension functions on PF2EParty to encapsulate flag-based persistence; KingdomActor is a plain typealias, not a subclass.

nodes.name: KingdomCharter.kt
nodes.summary: Defines RawCharter, loads the bundled charters JSON, and provides translateCharters() and getCharters() which merge homebrew overrides with the translated built-in charter list.

nodes.name: KingdomEvent.kt
nodes.summary: Defines raw JS-plain-object interfaces for kingdom events and their stages/outcomes, parses them into domain types, handles i18n translation of all text fields, and provides getEvents/getEvent helpers that merge homebrew overrides with built-in data.
nodes.languageNotes: Kotlin extension functions on RawKingdomEvent convert the JS plain object tree into strongly typed domain models; a two-pass translation handles @gainEvent button interpolation.

nodes.name: KingdomGovernment.kt
nodes.summary: Defines RawGovernment, loads the bundled governments JSON, and provides translateGovernments() and getGovernments() which merge homebrew overrides with the translated built-in government list.

nodes.name: KingdomHeartland.kt
nodes.summary: Defines RawHeartland, loads the bundled heartlands JSON, and provides translateHeartlands() and getHeartlands() which merge homebrew overrides with the translated built-in heartland list.

nodes.name: Leaders.kt
nodes.summary: Provides a single extension function on Foundry's Game object to retrieve the currently active kingdom leader from module settings.

nodes.name: HexContentSync.kt
nodes.summary: Synchronizes hex content markers (labelled rectangle drawings) onto the active Foundry scene, creating, updating, and deleting them in response to kingdom actor and scene update hooks.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Foundry hook callbacks via TypedHooks and coroutine-wrapped promises (buildPromise) for async drawing CRUD.

nodes.name: syncHexContentMarkers
nodes.summary: Reconciles all hex content drawing markers on the active scene against current kingdom hex contents, deleting stale markers and creating or updating one marker per populated hex.

nodes.name: registerHexContentSync
nodes.summary: Registers Foundry TypedHooks for actor update, scene update, and canvas-ready events to trigger hex content marker synchronisation.

nodes.name: HexGridSync.kt
nodes.summary: Manages all hex-grid overlay drawings on the active scene: claimed/explored/cleared polygon overlays, road segment drawings connecting adjacent road hexes, settlement name labels, and zone area labels, keeping them in sync with Kingmaker module state via Foundry hooks.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses inline js() blocks to call native Foundry grid APIs and compute polygon vertices; road segments are built as thin rectangle polygons via manual perpendicular-offset geometry.

nodes.name: registerHexGridSync
nodes.summary: Registers Foundry hooks (hex-edit close, actor update, scene update, canvas ready) to trigger the full suite of hex, settlement, and zone drawing syncs.

nodes.name: syncHexDrawingsToNativeState
nodes.summary: Full reconciliation pass that syncs claimed, explored, and cleared hex polygon overlays and road drawings to the active scene based on Kingmaker native hex state.

nodes.name: syncSettlementMarkers
nodes.summary: Creates or updates locked text drawings for each active settlement on the hex grid, matching settlement scene names to hex names and deleting orphaned markers.

nodes.name: syncZoneLabels
nodes.summary: Rebuilds zone label drawings by removing all existing zone labels and placing one text drawing per zone group at the geometric centroid of all its hexes.

nodes.name: RawKingdomFeature.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the JS-interop interface for raw kingdom feature data loaded from features.json and provides extension functions to explode multi-level features into per-level entries and to translate their display strings.

nodes.name: Realm.kt
nodes.summary: Resolves kingdom realm data (size and worksites) by three modes: reading Kingmaker module native hex state, scanning tile/drawing documents in a designated realm scene, or falling back to manually-entered kingdom data.

nodes.name: getRealmData
nodes.summary: Dispatches realm data resolution across the three automation modes (Kingmaker native, tile-based, or manual), returning a RealmData aggregate.

nodes.name: LayerDocuments.kt
nodes.summary: Defines a GridType enum distinguishing hex and square grids, and provides extension functions to convert TileDocument, TokenDocument, and DrawingDocument coordinates to Rectangle instances accounting for grid type.

nodes.name: Rectangle.kt
nodes.summary: Simple data class representing an axis-aligned rectangle with tolerance expansion and containment check, used for spatial hex/tile overlap calculations.

nodes.name: AbilityBoostContext.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the AbilityBoostContext view-model interface and provides a conversion function that maps raw ability boost choices to form element contexts (checkboxes or hidden inputs) for each kingdom ability.

nodes.name: BonusFeatContext.kt
nodes.summary: Defines view-model interfaces and factory functions for bonus feat selection and display contexts, including ruin threshold increase sub-contexts and leader vacancy penalty removal selectors.

nodes.name: CharterContext.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the CharterContext view-model and maps raw charter choices to a form context including a type selector and ability boost context based on the selected charter's fixed boost and free boost count.

nodes.name: FeaturesContext.kt
nodes.summary: Defines view-model interfaces for kingdom feature display grouped by level, and provides factory functions that build the full FeatureByLevelContext tree including feat selection dropdowns, ability boosts, ruin threshold increase controls, and skill proficiency selectors.

nodes.name: GovernmentContext.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the GovernmentContext view-model and converts raw government choices to a form context that surfaces the government type selector, associated feat details, skill proficiencies, ability boosts, and ruin threshold increase controls.

nodes.name: HeartlandContext.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the HeartlandContext view-model and maps raw heartland choices to a form context with a type selector dropdown, description, and ability boost label.

nodes.name: NewKingdomContext.kt
nodes.summary: Minimal view-model interface carrying only the new kingdom name, used when rendering the initial kingdom creation form.

nodes.name: OngoingEventContext.kt
nodes.summary: Defines view-model interfaces for ongoing kingdom events and their stage navigation, and provides an async coroutine-based factory that enriches event HTML, formats modifiers, and computes stage and settlement display data.

nodes.name: WorksitesContext.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the WorkSiteContext view-model and maps raw worksite data to form element contexts, rendering either editable number inputs or hidden inputs depending on whether resources are automated.

nodes.name: KingdomSheetDataModel.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the Foundry DataModel schema for the kingdom actor sheet, declaring the full field structure including stats, commodities, ruin, leaders, charter, government, features, bonus feats, companions, skill ranks, ability scores, and milestones.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the project's buildSchema DSL to declare nested Foundry DataModel field types; the @JsExport annotation exposes the class directly to Foundry's document system.

nodes.name: KingdomSheetDataModel
nodes.summary: Foundry DataModel subclass that declares the complete schema for the kingdom actor, covering all persistent kingdom sheet fields.

nodes.name: InitialValidation.kt
nodes.summary: On module load, validates all StructureActor items in the world against the structure-ref JSON schema and posts UI error notifications for any that fail, running only for the first GM.

nodes.name: RawStructureData.kt
nodes.summary: Defines JS-interop interfaces for all raw structure JSON fields (construction costs, bonus rules, commodity storage, etc.), loads structures.json and schema files as external modules, and provides translation and VK variant ID mapping utilities.

nodes.name: Structure.kt
nodes.summary: Provides extension functions to parse StructureActor and RawStructureData into strongly-typed Structure domain objects, resolve structure refs, and import structure actors from the module compendium pack.

nodes.name: parseStructure
nodes.summary: Converts a RawStructureData JS-interop object into a fully-typed Structure domain object, mapping all rule arrays, enum lookups, and optional fields.

nodes.name: importStructures
nodes.summary: Creates a Structures folder in the Foundry world and imports all structure NPC actors from the module compendium pack into it with world-owner permissions.

nodes.name: Validation.kt
nodes.summary: Validates structure JSON against the JSON schema using the optimumcode JsonSchema library, distinguishing structure-ref objects from full structure definitions and surfacing errors via StructureValidationError.

nodes.name: activities.hbs
nodes.summary: Handlebars template rendering a list of kingdom activities as collapsible detail elements, each showing action glyphs, skill list, description, degree-of-success outcomes, and a check or skip-collect-taxes action button.

nodes.name: army-browser.hbs
nodes.summary: Handlebars template for the army browser dialog, displaying an optional workbook army stats table and a main army list table with recruit buttons for each available army type.

nodes.name: army-tactics-browser.hbs
nodes.summary: Minimal Handlebars template rendering a table of available army tactics with level, DC, and a learn button that is disabled when the tactic is not currently trainable.

nodes.name: check.hbs
nodes.summary: Handlebars template for the kingdom check dialog, containing leader, skill, phase, and DC form inputs, an editable modifier table with add/delete rows, and roll or assurance action buttons that carry all modifier data as data attributes.

nodes.name: companion-profile.hbs
nodes.summary: Full read-only/GM profile view for a single companion: portrait, role/discovery badges, influence progress bar with GM +/- controls, camp-availability toggle, discovery-stage selector, plot-hook text, and a scrollable list of personal quests rendered via the companionQuestCard partial.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the companionQuestCard partial ({{> companionQuestCard}}) and conditionally gates all write controls behind {{#if isGM}}.

nodes.name: companion-quest-card.hbs
nodes.summary: Partial card component for a single companion personal quest, displaying title, status badge, description, quest hook, deadline turns remaining, influence reward, and GM-only visibility/complete/edit/delete action buttons.
nodes.languageNotes: Designed as a Handlebars partial consumed by companion-profile.hbs via {{> companionQuestCard}}.

nodes.name: companion-quest-row.hbs
nodes.summary: Compact single-row partial for displaying a companion quest in a list context, showing companion name, quest title, status, deadline, influence reward, and a GM button to open the companion's full profile.

nodes.name: consumption-breakdown.hbs
nodes.summary: Tooltip/dialog breakdown table for kingdom consumption, displaying how the current total is calculated from armies, settlements, modifiers, farmlands, and food reserves alongside resource and settlement surpluses.

nodes.name: event-browser.hbs
nodes.summary: Searchable event-picker dialog listing all available kingdom events as collapsible detail rows with trait tags, degree-of-success outcomes, resolution text, and buttons to add an event to the active session or generate a quest from it (GM only).

nodes.name: events.hbs
nodes.summary: Active kingdom-events list partial showing each ongoing event as an expandable row with multi-stage buttons, continuous-event toggle, resolve/roll button, and GM delete control; also embeds the quest-generator panel partial below the event list.
nodes.languageNotes: Embeds {{> kingdom-quest-generator}} at the bottom to render the quest generator panel inline with the events section.

nodes.name: generate-quest-dialog.hbs
nodes.summary: Full-screen quest generation dialog with a parchment-styled quest preview card (name, type, level, description, objectives, rewards) and an event-picker grid that lets the GM select an active event to generate from, commit the result, or cancel.
nodes.languageNotes: Reward pills cover XP, RP, Fame, Unrest reduction, commodity amounts, and custom rewards, making this one of the more data-dense dialog templates in the subsystem.

nodes.name: hex-content-add.hbs
nodes.summary: Minimal dialog template for adding new content to a specific hex, rendering the hex key as a heading and a generic formElement loop for the form fields with save/cancel actions.

nodes.name: hex-content-edit.hbs
nodes.summary: Minimal dialog template for editing existing hex content, structurally identical to hex-content-add.hbs but with an 'edit' heading label and the same formElement loop / save-cancel footer.

nodes.name: hex-content-manager.hbs
nodes.summary: Three-state manager panel for hex map content: shows an inline edit form, an inline add form, or the main list view with a data table of all entries (hexKey, type, name, visibility badge) and per-row edit/reveal-hide/clear/delete actions.

nodes.name: homebrew-profile-manager.hbs
nodes.summary: Generic manager table for homebrew data profiles (e.g. custom events, structures), listing each entry with name, id, version, created/updated timestamps, description, enable toggle, and edit/delete buttons.

nodes.name: kingdom-sheet.hbs
nodes.summary: Root layout template for the Kingdom Sheet ApplicationV2 window, rendering the header bar (name, fame, XP/level inputs), main tab navigation, and dispatching all content sections via named partials (character-sheet, notes, turn, trade-agreements, settlements, modifiers, quests, roster, party, army-pressure, pacing-alerts).
nodes.languageNotes: Acts as the top-level shell; all subsections are delegated to registered Handlebars partials, making this the compositional root of the kingdom sheet UI.

nodes.name: kingdom-size-help.hbs
nodes.summary: Read-only reference table tooltip showing kingdom size breakpoints with their nation type label, resource die, control DC modifier, and commodity storage cap.

nodes.name: population-add.hbs
nodes.summary: Dialog form for adding a new NPC to the kingdom population tracker, with fields for name, occupation (dropdown), and notes textarea, plus save/cancel action buttons.

nodes.name: population-edit.hbs
nodes.summary: Dialog form for editing an existing NPC population entry, pre-populating name, occupation, and notes from context data, with save/delete/cancel action buttons.

nodes.name: quest-card-generated-badge.hbs
nodes.summary: Micro partial rendering an inline badge span indicating that a quest was AI-generated, optionally showing the source event name it was generated from.

nodes.name: quest-generator-settings.hbs
nodes.summary: Settings dialog for the quest generator, rendering a generic formElement loop for configurable options (e.g. model, style) with save/cancel footer buttons.

nodes.name: quest-generator.hbs

tour.title: Kingdom Actor Root
tour.description: The subsystem begins with Kingdom.kt, which defines KingdomActor as a typealias for PF2EParty and exposes getKingdom/setKingdom/clearKingdom extension functions. These three functions are the single read-write interface to all kingdom state: every engine, sheet, and dialog ultimately calls them to fetch or persist KingdomData stored as Foundry actor flags. Understanding this gateway first makes every layer above it legible.
tour.languageLesson: Kotlin typealiases (typealias KingdomActor = PF2EParty) let you give domain-meaningful names to external types without wrapping them in a new class. Extension functions defined on that alias then provide a clean API boundary without subclassing a JS-interop type.

tour.title: The Kingdom State Schema
tour.description: KingdomData.kt defines the central KingdomData and KingdomSettings @JsPlainObject interfaces — the in-memory representation of everything a kingdom tracks: ability scores, skill ranks, leaders, resources, commodities, ruin, feats, settlements, armies, quests, pacing alerts, and campaign clock. With 23 fan-in references this is the most-depended-upon data node in the subsystem. KingdomSheetDataModel.kt mirrors this structure as the Foundry DataModel schema for actor-flag validation, declaring which fields Foundry must persist. Reading both files together shows exactly what shape the JSON stored on the PF2EParty actor takes.
tour.languageLesson: @JsPlainObject in Kotlin/JS generates a plain JavaScript object literal interface with no class overhead — the resulting JS is safe to pass directly to Foundry's setFlag/getFlag APIs. Extension functions on these interfaces let you add computed properties without polluting the serialized shape.

tour.title: JS Data Contracts
tour.description: The data/ package contains all the fine-grained @JsPlainObject sub-interfaces that compose KingdomData. RawResources and RawConsumption model the now/next resource buckets (with an endTurn extension that rolls them forward), RawCharacter captures companion roster entries with influence and quest tracking, and RawWarThreat and RawArmyDeployment define the war-board entries that feed the Army Pressure system introduced in Step 9. These contracts are the canonical serialization schema: changing a field name here is a migration event.

tour.title: The Modifier DSL
tour.description: The domain-core layer (commonMain/) provides the Foundry-free modifier engine. Modifier.kt defines the core data class carrying type, value, conditional expression, roll options, and fortune/upgrade flags — it is the most imported file in the entire graph with 29 fan-in edges. ModifierType.kt enumerates the eight PF2e modifier categories (ABILITY, PROFICIENCY, ITEM, STATUS, CIRCUMSTANCE, LEADERSHIP, VACANCY, UNTYPED) with i18n keys. Expression.kt defines the sealed Expression<T> interface requiring an evaluate(ExpressionContext) method; concrete implementations (Eq, Gt, In, When, All, Some, etc.) allow modifier predicates to be serialized as JSON and evaluated against live kingdom state at roll-time.
tour.languageLesson: Kotlin sealed interfaces let the compiler enforce exhaustive when() branches — every Expression subtype must be handled. Combined with Kotlin/Multiplatform (commonMain), this DSL compiles to both JVM (for tests) and JS (for Foundry) from a single source set, with zero platform-specific code.

tour.title: Modifier Evaluation Pipeline
tour.description: The evaluation sub-package in commonMain/ implements the full modifier resolution pipeline. CreateAllModifiers.kt is the aggregation root: it calls all bonus factories (proficiency, ability, leader, structure, invested, repair, ruler, leadership) and penalty factories (unrest, ruin, vacancy, anarchy, army conditions, no-bridge, favored-land) to assemble the complete modifier list from kingdom state. FilterModifiers.kt then narrows that list to those matching a skill/activity selector and whose applyIf expression evaluates true in the current context. EvaluateModifiers.kt applies PF2e stacking rules (highest per typed bonus, lowest penalty per type, all UNTYPED stack) and returns a ModifierResult with the final bonus total, breakdown, and fortune/upgrade flags.

tour.title: Resource Math & Unrest Formulas
tour.description: Also in commonMain/, three pure-function files implement the economic and social formulas that feed both the turn engine and sheet calculations. Consumption.kt (resources/) defines the Consumption data class and calculateConsumption, tallying settlement, army, and modifier-based food costs against farmland to compute the net food deficit. Income.kt derives raw commodity gains and resource dice from worksites and kingdom size. Unrest.kt computes a GainedUnrest breakdown — from overcrowding, war status, secondary territory, and vacant ruler — that the sheet's CalculateUnrest layer applies to the kingdom each turn. All three files share no Foundry dependencies and are directly unit-testable.

tour.title: Structure & Settlement Evaluation
tour.description: EvaluateStructures.kt is the bridge between the physical city-builder layer and the modifier engine. Given a list of raw structures placed in a settlement, it resolves consumption reductions, aggregates the highest unique structure bonuses into ITEM modifiers (used by the StructureBonuses factory in Step 5), computes available item groups, and assembles a fully-evaluated Settlement domain object. KingdomModifier.kt (in jsMain) is the JS-target companion: it declares raw JS-interop interfaces for modifier JSON, provides parse/serialize functions, and exposes checkModifiers and createExpressionContext — the two functions KingdomSheet calls to assemble all active modifiers and evaluation context from a live KingdomData.

tour.title: Monthly Turn Ticking Engine
tour.description: TurnTickingEngine.kt is the pure-domain heart of the monthly kingdom turn. Implemented as a Kotlin singleton object with no Foundry dependencies, it processes all end-turn state transitions in a single deterministic function: fame advancement, resource/consumption rollover (using the now/next pattern from Step 3), commodity storage capping, council cooldowns, modifier expiry, campaign clock tick, quest timer decrement, and war threat/pressure recalculation. Its Foundry-free design means the full End Turn logic is covered by TurnTickingEngineTest.kt with 15+ test cases, making regressions immediately visible.
tour.languageLesson: Kotlin object declarations create singletons with no constructor overhead. Combining this with a Kotlin/JS target lets you write pure business logic once in commonMain (or jsMain without Foundry calls) and run it under Node.js in jsTest — the same byte-code that ships to the browser runs in the test harness.

tour.title: Pacing & War Pressure Systems
tour.description: Two pure-domain files implement the campaign health monitors introduced in roadmap phases #12 and #13. PacingAlerts.kt evaluates four pacing conditions (level mismatch, unrest stagnation, turn gap, loot imbalance) against KingdomSettings thresholds and emits RawPacingAlerts only on threshold crossings, with fire-once semantics to suppress repeat spam. ArmyWarPressure.kt calculates cumulative war pressure from active RawWarThreats and supporting army deployments, advances the threat escalation clock each turn, and exposes KingdomSettings accessors for configurable thresholds. Both are tested exhaustively — PacingAlertsTest.kt covers all four evaluators and their stateful tracker counterparts; ArmyWarPressureTest.kt covers pressure accumulation, army reduction, ETA countdown, and the soft-pause expiry mechanic.

tour.title: Sheet Orchestration Layer
tour.description: KingdomSheet.kt is the ApplicationV2 god object (fan-out: 35 imports) that wires all subsystems to the Foundry UI. Its collaborators in the sheet/ package divide the work: BeforeKingdomUpdate handles pre-save validation (feat ruin-threshold cleanup, ability boost resets, milestone XP, ruin breach alerts); CalculateIncome, CalculateUnrest, and Consumption execute the economic sub-phases of End Turn with Foundry chat output; Xp implements level-up logic with chat feedback. KingdomSheetData declares the top-level JsPlainObject that Handlebars receives, and Defaults provides the createKingdomDefaults factory for new kingdoms. Together these files represent the Foundry-coupled 'application boundary' — everything above this layer is pure domain or pure template.

tour.title: View-Model Contexts
tour.description: The sheet/contexts/ package contains pure Handlebars context builders — Foundry-free functions that map raw KingdomData and domain objects to typed interfaces the templates consume directly. KingdomSheetContext.kt is the top-level aggregator; below it, ActivitiesContext resolves per-activity skill validity and groups activities by phase, SkillChecksContext computes effective bonuses for every kingdom skill, ArmyPressureContext localizes the war board data for the army-pressure tab, PacingAlertContext localizes severity labels and alert messages, TurnWizardContext declares the turn-wizard checklist and state-summary interfaces, and ConsumptionBreakdownContext converts the Consumption domain object to a template-ready view model. Because these builders have no Foundry calls, they are unit-tested directly — see CompanionProfileContextTest.kt for the pattern.

tour.title: Key Dialogs
tour.description: KingdomCheckDialog.kt is the busiest interactive surface: it assembles the full modifier list (via KingdomModifier from Step 7), renders editable modifier pills with fortune/assurance/creative-solution toggles, resolves the activity DC, and fires the roll. TurnWizardApplication.kt implements the end-turn wizard dialog and the performEndTurn top-level function, presenting a turn checklist, state summary, activity-cap validation, and tick preview before calling TurnTickingEngine.tick() on commit. These two dialogs show the full call chain from user gesture to domain mutation: dialog → sheet context → engine → TurnTickingEngine → KingdomData → setKingdom.

tour.title: Handlebars Templates
tour.description: The Handlebars layer translates the context objects from Step 11 into HTML. kingdom-sheet.hbs is the root layout: it renders the header bar and dispatches all 12 content sections via named partials. sections/turn/page.hbs is the most complex partial, hosting upkeep, commerce, leadership, region, civic, army, event, quest-timers, clocks, XP/milestones, and end-turn sub-sections. check.hbs drives the modifier table in KingdomCheckDialog: each row is an input binding that carries modifier data as data-attributes for the roll button. sections/army-pressure/page.hbs and sections/pacing-alerts/page.hbs render the war board and balance-alerts tabs respectively. Handlebars helper calls and partial composition ({{> partial-name}}) are the only logic here — all decision-making happened in the context builders.
tour.languageLesson: Foundry's ApplicationV2 + Handlebars convention separates rendering concerns cleanly: Kotlin context builders produce a plain JS object, Handlebars templates consume it with {{expression}} interpolation and {{#each}} / {{#if}} blocks, and named partials (registered in Main.kt loadTemplatePartials) allow the sheet to compose sections without duplicating markup.
